whyThisMatters: A password built from a name and a birth year can be guessed in seconds — length, randomness and mixed types are what actually slow an attacker down, not personal cleverness.
rememberThis: Longer and more random beats clever every time — use a phrase, not a name + year.

discussionPrompts: Ask the room to compare their built password's strength meter to their actual personal password habits — any uncomfortable honesty there?
Ask why length matters more than adding one symbol — can anyone explain it in their own words after watching the meter move?
Ask if anyone has ever reused a "strong" password across multiple accounts, and why that undoes the strength.
facilitatorNotes.commonWrongAnswer: Stopping as soon as the meter turns green — adding just one symbol or number instead of pushing for length — is the most common miss; participants consistently undervalue length over complexity.
